summary.en: Reference for the KERN layout helper classes: flex container and item classes, CSS Grid utilities whose .kern-grid wrapper replaces the legacy .kern-row grid, the container and container-fluid wrappers, gap and spacing classes using the .kern-{property}{sides}-{size}[-{breakpoint}] scheme, stack, visibility and display helpers, and size, aspect-ratio and overflow classes. All classes are mobile first; breakpoints are sm 576px, md 768px, lg 992px, xl 1200px and xxl 1600px.
Utilities for flex containers and items. Most properties accept a breakpoint suffix, for example .kern-flex-row-md.
Classes for display and direction: .kern-flex, .kern-inline-flex, .kern-flex-row[-{breakpoint}], .kern-flex-row-reverse, .kern-flex-col, .kern-flex-col-reverse, .kern-flex-wrap and .kern-flex-nowrap.

Breakpoint-capable justify-content classes on the main axis (start, end, center, between, around, evenly) and align-items classes on the cross axis (start, end, center, stretch, baseline), for example .kern-justify-content-between-lg. An example switches from row on mobile to column at md.
Controls the order of flex items, also per breakpoint: .kern-order-{0-12}[-{breakpoint}], .kern-order-first (order: -9999) and .kern-order-last (order: 9999), for example .kern-order-2-sm.

Low-level access to CSS Grid for complex layouts without custom CSS. A wrapper .kern-grid defines the grid with display: grid and replaces the classic .kern-row architecture; columns and gaps are set through modifier classes.

Grid display classes: .kern-grid (display: grid, default 12 columns and gap-lg) and .kern-inline-grid. Column and row counts come from .kern-grid-cols-{n} (1-12) and .kern-grid-rows-{n} (1-6); gaps from .kern-gap-{size}[-{breakpoint}], also .kern-gap-x-{size} and .kern-gap-y-{size}.
Places items in the grid: .kern-col-{n}[-{breakpoint}] spans n columns, .kern-col-start-{n} and .kern-col-end-{n} set the start or end column line.
Example that creates three equally wide columns across all viewports.
Responsive suffixes adapt the layout; the example starts with 2 columns on mobile and switches to 4 columns from the md breakpoint.
Defines the basic grid structure on the container.
Controls the gap between columns and rows.
Grid items wrap automatically onto the next row once more than the available 12 columns are occupied.
Replaces traditional offsets: it states explicitly where an element starts or ends.

Items without an explicit column class occupy one unit of the 12-column grid by default. .kern-col-auto sizes an item from its content but keeps it inside the grid: in CSS Grid it takes exactly one grid cell regardless of content width.
Grids can be nested without limit. The inner grid does not inherit the parent's column count; it defines a new grid context.
All classes follow the mobile-first approach.
Do use kern-gap to define spacing, and kern-col-full for elements that should break out of the grid. Do not mix kern-row (legacy) with kern-grid syntax.

.kern-container is a primary layout element: it centres the whole page content horizontally and limits it to a readable maximum width. It should be the direct child of the body tag or of the main layout area.

.kern-container-fluid is a variant without a max-width: it always takes the full viewport width at every breakpoint. It is typically used to keep the horizontal padding at the page edges while content fills the available area, ideal for elements that must span the full width.

Centring via margin-left and margin-right set to auto; a max-width bound to the breakpoints so content does not become unreadably wide on large screens; horizontal padding so content does not stick to the browser edges, especially on small viewports.
Gap classes space flex and grid elements through the gap property, without extra margins or paddings. All KERN spaces can be used as values.

Margin and padding classes follow .kern-{property}{sides}-{size}[-{breakpoint}]: property m or p; sides empty (all), t, b, l, r, x (horizontal) or y (vertical); a size; and an optional breakpoint. Examples: .kern-m-md, .kern-pt-lg, .kern-p-lg-sm (large padding from the small breakpoint).

Same breakpoints as the grid system: no suffix is always active (mobile first), -sm from 576px, -md from 768px, -lg from 992px, -xl from 1200px, -xxl from 1600px. kern-mx-auto centres a block element with a fixed width.

.kern-stack is a vertical flex container with the standard md gap. .kern-stack-{size} changes the spacing for all screen sizes; sizes are none, xxs, xs, sm, md, lg, xl. .kern-stack-{size}-{breakpoint} makes it responsive.
Stack supports unlimited nesting, which allows flexible layout hierarchies on one page.

Display classes with breakpoints, e.g. .kern-hidden-sm: .kern-block, .kern-flex, .kern-inline-block, .kern-inline, .kern-hidden. .kern-sr-only is screen-reader only; .kern-sr-only-mobile hides on mobile (up to 767px), shows on desktop. .kern-overflow-{auto|hidden|visible|scroll} sets overflow.
Classes for the dimensions (width, height) and aspect ratio of elements. All are responsive and take a suffix such as -md or -lg, for example .kern-w-full-lg.
Use .kern-w/h-full for 100% of the parent size and .kern-w/h-screen for 100% of the viewport size.
.kern-min-h-screen is often used in layouts to make sure content fills at least the screen height.
The .kern-aspect-* classes force an element to keep a fixed aspect ratio even when its width changes.
These classes decide what happens when an element's content is larger than the element itself, and are typically used on containers. .kern-overflow-auto is the recommended default in most cases.
KERN layout utilities: flex, CSS Grid (.kern-grid replaces kern-row), container, gap/spacing, stack, visibility and size classes with mobile-first breakpoints.

whenToUse.en: Use .kern-container to centre page content and cap it at a readable width; place it as the direct child of body or the main layout area.
Use .kern-container-fluid for elements that must span the full viewport width.
Use .kern-stack to arrange elements vertically with consistent spacing.

dos.en: Define spacing with kern-gap instead of adding margins between grid items.
Use kern-col-full for elements that should break out of the grid.

donts.en: Do not mix the legacy kern-row syntax with kern-grid.
